title: Head tracking tutorial on After Effects

skills.name: Subject-locked head stabilization

what.objective: Hold a hero subject's head in a stable viewer-space region while allowing the surrounding shot motion to become the visible movement, then repair stabilization edge exposure and residual harshness.

components.visibleResult: A stable high-contrast facial/head feature is tracked across the shot.
components.role: Provide reliable motion evidence for subject locking.
interactions: Drives inverse stabilization and determines whether the edit remains credible.

components.visibleResult: The hero head remains approximately locked while the background moves around it.
components.role: Create the defining subject-locked visual gesture.
interactions: Depends on track quality and creates border exposure that later edge treatment must handle.

components.visibleResult: Compensating motion does not reveal distracting black edges.
components.role: Preserve frame coverage after inverse motion.
interactions: Should be no stronger than required; excessive tiling can create repeated-edge artifacts.

components.visibleResult: Scale and position are adjusted so the locked head remains compositionally intentional rather than merely mathematically stationary.
components.role: Restore visual hierarchy and crop safety after stabilization.
interactions: Balances edge coverage against facial readability and aspect-ratio constraints.

components.visibleResult: Residual micro-jitter and hard frame cadence are softened without visibly smearing the face.
interactions: Motion blur and frame blending are finishing tools, not substitutes for a bad track.

whenWhy.creativeIntent: Turn subject motion and camera movement into a stylized subject-lock where the hero face becomes the visual anchor.
whenWhy.attentionGoal: Keep viewer attention fixed on the hero head while environmental motion supplies energy.
whenWhy.emotionalPurpose: Create a controlled, dominant, edit-forward feeling in which the subject appears visually anchored despite motion.
whenWhy.pacingRole: Works best as a short emphasis passage or transition-supporting shot; the locked anchor can make surrounding motion feel more energetic without adding shake.
whenWhy.musicRelationship: Can support a musical accent or energetic section, but the lock itself is driven by subject motion continuity rather than requiring a beat.
whenWhy.dialogueRelationship: Avoid aggressive locking or smoothing when facial articulation and natural camera continuity are more important than stylized emphasis.
motionConditions: A persistent high-contrast feature near the hero head remains trackable for the intended window.
Subject/camera motion is large enough that stabilizing around the head produces a meaningful environmental-motion effect.
Occlusion, strong profile rotation, motion blur, or feature deformation do not invalidate the chosen point.
compositionConditions: The hero head can remain inside a safe composition region after compensation.
Enough crop headroom exists to hide stabilization borders without destroying subject readability.
Mirrored/tiled edge content will not create obvious duplicate objects or seams.
continuityConstraints: Do not erase intentional camera motion when continuity depends on the original move.
Do not let subject-locking create an implausible jump at shot boundaries.
If track confidence collapses, repair or shorten the window rather than hiding drift with blur.
useWhen: A hero face/head is the dominant attention target and a stylized locked-subject look fits the edit.
The shot contains useful relative motion that becomes visually interesting when the subject is stabilized.
A short energetic passage benefits from stronger subject anchoring than ordinary reframing.
avoidWhen: The track feature is frequently occluded, deforming, low-contrast, or leaving frame.
Natural handheld/camera motion is narratively important and should remain visible.
The required scale or edge fill would crop important anatomy or reveal obvious repeated-edge artifacts.
Face detail would be degraded by the motion blur/frame blending needed to hide residual errors.
whenWhy.restraintRule: Use the smallest stabilization window, crop/scale compensation, edge fill, and temporal smoothing that creates a convincing lock; if the subject already reads clearly, no effect can be better than forcing the technique.

topology: One hero AV layer is selected as the stabilization target.
Native Stabilize Motion uses one track point for Position-only stabilization.
The track feature is placed on a persistent high-contrast head/face detail and analyzed forward.
Apply uses X and Y dimensions, producing inverse position compensation around the tracked feature.
Motion Tile is added after stabilization when compensation exposes borders; mirrored edges are enabled and output coverage is expanded only as needed.
Layer transform position/scale is then reframed around the hero head and crop-safe region.
Layer/composition motion blur and frame blending are enabled only when visual review shows they improve residual cadence without smearing the face.
how.timingModel: Tracking and stabilization span only the useful subject-lock window; reframe and edge coverage are derived from the maximum compensation over that same window rather than copied from tutorial constants.
how.easingModel: Native stabilization compensation follows measured motion rather than an authored ease curve; any reframe adjustment should avoid adding competing animated drift unless intentionally designed.
adaptationRules: Choose a track feature for persistence and local contrast, not because it occupies the tutorial's literal sunglasses/nose coordinates.
Shorten or repair the tracked window when confidence drops, occlusion appears, or the feature changes shape materially.
Derive border coverage from measured compensation amplitude, aspect ratio, and crop headroom before choosing scale or mirrored edge expansion.
Prefer crop/scale compensation when it is visually cheap; use mirrored Motion Tile only when edge exposure remains and duplicate-edge artifacts are unlikely.
Reframe toward the semantic hero-head safe region rather than blindly centering the source layer.
Enable motion blur/frame blending only after track and reframe quality pass; reduce or disable them if facial detail smears.
The literal Motion Tile implementation uses the stable first-party match name ADBE Tile; property values remain adaptive rather than copied.

mechanisms.intent: Measure persistent hero-head motion and apply inverse X/Y position compensation so the head becomes the viewer-space anchor.
mechanisms.construction: Use native Stabilize Motion in Position mode with one persistent high-contrast head/face feature, Analyze Forward, then Apply X and Y. Verify tracker sample growth plus Anchor Point compensation readback rather than trusting UI completion alone.
mechanisms.observableResult: The selected head feature remains approximately fixed while the environment moves around it.

parameters.name: stabilizationMode
parameters.intent: Restrict the tutorial technique to position locking unless rotation/scale evidence explicitly requires more.

parameters.name: analysisDirection
parameters.intent: Analyze in the proven direction for the selected shot window.

parameters.name: trackFeaturePolicy
parameters.intent: Choose a persistent high-contrast feature near the hero head rather than a fixed coordinate.

parameters.name: minimumTrackConfidence
parameters.intent: Fail closed or repair instead of accepting visible drift.

mechanisms.intent: Prevent stabilization compensation from revealing black frame edges while minimizing repeated-edge artifacts.
mechanisms.construction: Add first-party Motion Tile (matchName ADBE Tile). Use stable property paths for output coverage and Mirror Edges; expand only enough to cover measured border exposure.
mechanisms.observableResult: No black borders appear during the lock and mirrored edge content does not become a visible pattern.

parameters.name: effectMatchName
parameters.intent: Select the native Motion Tile implementation without relying on localized display text.

parameters.name: mirrorEdges
parameters.intent: Mirror boundary pixels instead of exposing transparent/black borders.

parameters.name: outputExpansion
parameters.intent: Expand tile output only enough to cover compensation amplitude.

parameters.name: edgeArtifactTolerance
parameters.intent: Limit expansion when mirrored duplicates become perceptually obvious.

mechanisms.intent: Restore intentional composition after stabilization by placing the hero head inside a crop-safe attention region.
mechanisms.construction: Adjust native layer Position and Scale after stabilization using hero-head location, crop headroom, edge exposure, and aspect ratio; do not copy tutorial coordinates.
mechanisms.observableResult: The locked head sits in an intentional frame position with sufficient coverage and readable facial scale.

parameters.name: position
parameters.intent: Place the hero head in a semantic safe region appropriate to the shot.

parameters.name: scale
parameters.intent: Use an adapted native scale vector that preserves coverage and subject hierarchy without copying tutorial percentages.

mechanisms.intent: Polish residual motion cadence after a good lock without using blur to conceal tracking failure.
mechanisms.construction: Enable the already-proven composition/layer motion controls and choose frame blending only when visual review benefits. The tutorial visibly enables motion blur and frame blending after the structural work.
mechanisms.observableResult: Micro-jitter feels smoother while facial details remain legible.

parameters.name: motionBlurEnabled
parameters.intent: Enable layer motion blur only when residual motion benefits.

parameters.name: frameBlendingType
parameters.intent: Choose a concrete AE frame-blending mode from cadence and artifact risk.

parameters.name: compMotionBlurEnabled
parameters.intent: Enable composition motion-blur rendering when the layer uses motion blur.

parameters.name: compFrameBlendingEnabled
parameters.intent: Enable composition frame blending only when the selected layer mode requires it.

parameters.name: shutterAngle
parameters.intent: Preserve or adapt the composition shutter angle for readable facial motion.

parameters.name: shutterPhase
parameters.intent: Preserve or adapt shutter phase without introducing temporal bias.

parameters.name: samplesPerFrame
parameters.intent: Use enough samples for smooth motion without unnecessary render cost.

parameters.name: adaptiveSampleLimit
parameters.intent: Bound adaptive sampling according to motion complexity and render budget.

capabilityRequirements.reason: Execute the retained native position Stabilize Motion Analyze Forward + Apply workflow with verified visual target binding.
Verify tracker samples and compensation keyframes before/after the guarded stabilization action.
Add native Motion Tile using stable matchName ADBE Tile.
Set Motion Tile output coverage and Mirror Edges through stable effect property paths.
Apply subject-aware position and scale compensation after stabilization.
Enable composition motion rendering controls when needed.
Enable layer motion blur and select frame blending mode.

validationCriteria: The hero head remains perceptually locked through the intended window without obvious drift.
No black/transparent borders appear after stabilization compensation.
Motion Tile or crop compensation does not create distracting repeated-edge patterns.
The post-lock reframe preserves face readability and intentional composition.
Motion blur/frame blending improve cadence without smearing the hero face or hiding track errors.
The technique remains recognizably subject-locked when transferred to footage with a different head position, motion direction, frame rate, and aspect ratio.
invariants: Position stabilization uses a semantically bound hero-head feature and refuses unresolved/low-confidence identity.
The retained tutorial route is Position X/Y only; rotation/scale stabilization is not silently assumed.
Stabilization truth is verified from tracker and compensation-key growth, not only UI completion.
Edge-fill strength is derived from measured exposure and crop headroom rather than fixed tutorial percentages.
Reframe does not move the hero head outside the declared safe region.
Temporal smoothing is downstream of structural lock quality and cannot convert a failed track into a pass.

failureModes.condition: The head slowly drifts or suddenly jumps while the background appears stable.
failureModes.diagnosis: The chosen feature lost persistence, analysis drifted, or an occlusion/deformation invalidated the point.
failureModes.repairStrategy: Repair/reseed the track around the failure or shorten the stabilization window; do not increase blur first.

failureModes.condition: Black borders or transparent wedges appear during larger compensation.
failureModes.diagnosis: Scale/crop coverage and edge-fill output are insufficient for the measured stabilization offset.
failureModes.repairStrategy: Increase crop-safe scale or adaptive Motion Tile output only as much as necessary, then recheck edge artifacts.

failureModes.condition: Repeated faces/objects or mirrored seams appear at frame edges.
failureModes.diagnosis: Motion Tile expansion is too aggressive for salient edge content.
failureModes.repairStrategy: Prefer additional crop/scale, reduce tile expansion, shorten the lock window, or choose a different shot/feature.

failureModes.condition: The head is technically stable but composition feels awkward.
failureModes.diagnosis: Inverse motion was applied without a semantic reframe around hero position, gaze, and aspect ratio.
failureModes.repairStrategy: Recompute target head safe region and scale/position compensation before altering the track.

failureModes.condition: The face looks smeared or rubbery.
failureModes.diagnosis: Motion blur or frame blending is too strong for facial detail or occlusion.
failureModes.repairStrategy: Reduce/disable temporal smoothing and preserve the clean stabilized result.

transferAxes: different subject/camera motion direction and amplitude
different facial feature selected for tracking
different border exposure and crop headroom
robustnessAxes: high motion blur or low local contrast
feature leaving frame near the lock boundary
edge content that makes mirror tiling visibly repetitive

scenePrerequisites: A hero subject/head can be semantically identified with enough confidence to bind the stabilization target.
At least one persistent high-contrast head/face feature can be tracked for the intended window.
The shot has enough crop headroom or safe edge-fill content to absorb inverse-motion border exposure.
The stylized subject-lock fits the narrative/continuity role of the shot.

newConcepts: Subject-locked stabilization is a distinct semantic primitive from tracking: tracking measures motion; stabilization applies inverse motion to make a chosen feature the viewer-space anchor.
Stabilization requires an explicit edge-coverage policy because successful inverse motion can create new border defects.
reinforcedConcepts: Professional tracking target selection is semantic and confidence-driven rather than coordinate memorization.
Motion blur and frame blending are finishing primitives and should not mask structural failure.
newCombinations: Guarded native position stabilization + adaptive Motion Tile edge coverage + subject-aware reframe + selective temporal smoothing.
refinements: The existing M4 stabilization capability is directly reusable; no tutorial-specific tracking adapter is needed.
Native Motion Tile can use generic effect-add/property-set access rather than a dedicated tutorial function.
contradictions: The tutorial calls the result head tracking, but the visible AE construction is native position stabilization around a tracked head feature, not an attachment-follow recipe such as text or graphics parented to tracking data.
